# Contributing

Bug fixes, features, plugin work, and documentation improvements are all
welcome.
The rules below keep the architecture coherent - every
contribution should make the system **more** self-consistent, not less.

## 1. Core principles

- **One logical piece at a time.** Do not bundle an unrelated refactor,
  a dependency upgrade, and a bug fix into one change - it is impossible to
  review or roll back safely.
- **Permission default = ASK.** Never push, open a PR, merge, rebase, or
  ev en commit to `origin` without explicit approval from Sofia.
  Local git
  actions are also off-limits without approval; the maintainers handle
  git directly.
- **Never edit code you have not read in the current session.** If a file
  has drifted, re-read it first.
- **Plan before big changes.** Non-trivial work lives in `.opencode/plans/`
  - keep `tasklog.md` per-task and `projectlog.md` per-project current.
- **No live-model or live-provider tests.** `ALLOW_MODEL_REQUESTS=False`
  in `tests/conftest.py` is never bypassed - tests use mocks only.
  Real
  providers are exercised manually in the browser or TUI.

## 2. Development setup

### Workspace

1. The working tree is everything - `.berg-agents/` (config, sessions,
   memory), `sharedtodos/` (user tasks), and `.opencode/` (plans, notes)
   are git-ignored but shared for continuity.
   Do not delete them.
2. Node and Bun are not always on `PATH` (shell is non-interactive).
   Use absolute binaries (e.g. `~/.bun/bin/bun`,
   `~/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin/node`).
3. Use `uv` for all Python environment and dependency work.

### First-time install

```bash
uv venv
cd .venv  # implied by project root
source .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install -e .
```

### Front-end (once, then on change)

```bash
cd berg_agents/ui/webapp
npm install   # or: bun install
npm run build # static export served by FastAPI on one origin
```

### Plugin bundles (shared-todo and any others)

```bash
cd berg_plugins/<plugin>
npm install
npm run build:ui     # writes ui/dist/<surface>.js if the manifest declares an entry
```

### Configuration

- Copy/adapt `.berg-agents/bergagents.jsonc` and put secrets in `.env`
  under `${env:VAR_NAME}` references - never in source.
- Verify the active config dir with `BERG_AGENTS_CONFIG_DIR` before you
  assume a data location.

## 3. Where code lives

  | Area           | Location                           | Notes                                                                 |
  | ---            | ---                                | ---                                                                   |
  | Harness/agents | `berg_agents/agents/`              | `AbstractAgent`, Guardian, Planner, Implementation, Curator, Learning |
  | Tools (specs)  | `berg_agents/agents/factory.py`    | `ToolSpec` values, risk classes, native + MCP tools                   |
  | Web + TUI      | `berg_agents/ui/`                  | `server.py`, `routes.py`, `session_store.py`, FastAPI helpers         |
  | Web front-end  | `berg_agents/ui/webapp/app/`       | Next.js, HeroUI, plugins, runtime (`BergRuntime`)                     |
  | Plugin system  | `berg_agents/plugin_system/`       | discovery, capabilities, memory, compaction, sessions                 |
  | Providers      | `berg_agents/providers/`           | provider-centric resolution - never add a global provider flag        |
  | Config         | `berg_agents/config/`              | single resolver in `paths.py`; settings, config manager               |
  | Plugins        | `berg_plugins/<plugin-id>/`        | one home per plugin (manifest, code, UI bundle)                       |
  | Docs           | `docs/*.qmd`, `docs/plugins/*.qmd` | Quarto source; `README.md` generated from `README.qmd`                |

## 4. Architecture rules you must respect

1. **Config single source of truth.** All config files resolve through
   `berg_agents/config/paths.resolve_config_dir` - mirror one logic means
   no hard-coded `.berg-agents`/`.berg-config` strings elsewhere.
2. **Provider-centric config.** A model carries its own provider,
   `baseURL`, and `apiKey`.
   No global provider flag, EVER.
3. **Plugin installing must not require a host edit.** Plugins ship a built
   JS bundle; the host imports the plugin source in no place - it only
   mounts manifest-declared UI at runtime.
   Adding a plugin line to
   `registry.tsx` is a known gap to fix, not acceptable architecture.
4. **User data is inviolable.** `sharedtodos/` is her data - never
   auto-delete, rewrite cache, or reformat it as a \"clean-up\" step.
   Older
   nested memory files were explicitly left in place for manual merge.
5. **Memory path is flat.** `FileStore` rooted at the config directory,
   namespace empty, `agent_name=\"memory\"` so `MEMORY.md` lands at
   `{config}/memory/MEMORY.md`.
   Double-nesting is a known regression.
6. **Compaction ordering is load-bearing.** Compaction (mutable history)
   is registered **before** `Memory` (request-only injection) - otherwise
   a memory block is dropped by the rewrite.
   Do not re-order.
7. **Session store is per-operation connections.** sqlite3 thread affinity;
   do not cache connections across asyncio tasks.
8. **Permission default = ask** for tools surfaced in chat (high-risk /
   HITL) and for any agent that runs unsafe steps.
9. **Comments must stay** - source comments are clarity, not \"AI slop\".

## 5. Adding a tool

1. Implement the function in `berg_agents/agents/` (or as a `ToolCapability`
   in a plugin).
2. Wrap it as `make_tool_spec(... name=..., risk_class=low|high ...)` so it
   inherits atomic writes, timeouts, path normalization.
3. Add it to `create_tools()` (or the plugin capability registrations).
4. Declare its HITL class implicitly by `risk_class`: high-risk auto-gates.
5. Write tests under `tests/` using mocks only; do not forward to live
   providers.
6. Document it in `docs/TOOLS.qmd` and (if user-facing) `FAQ.qmd`.

## 6. Writing a plugin

Follow `berg_plugins/shared-todo/` as the conformance baseline:

1. `plugin.yaml` with `metadata`, `entry`, `capabilities`, and - if the
   plugin has UI - a `ui:` block (`entry`, `export`, `placement`, `label`,
   `width`).
2. Real `BergPlugin` subclass imported from `berg_agents.plugin_system`
   (no local stubs).
3. `PluginContext` is populated via `load_config` with schema defaults so
   config is alive - never read env/config manually in the entry point.
4. Capabilities are stored persistently: use `persist=True` for
   per-plugin identity fields (skill path / MCP server name etc.).
5. Ship a built bundle produced by esbuild (`build-ui.mjs`); treat
   React/ReactDOM/component libraries as **externals** against
   `window.BergRuntime` so there is exactly one React instance.
6. Use `apiBase()` from the runtime helper - never bake `process.env`
   into the bundle.
   SetCache-Control is handled by the host, but keep the
   URL stable and rebuild freely.
7. Give the plugin UI the `PluginSurfaceProps` contract (`view`,
   `refreshKey`, etc.).
   Tries on `refreshKey` is how it stays in sync.

See `docs/plugins/PLUGIN-UI.qmd` and `docs/plugins/SHARED-TODO.qmd` for
the full contract.

## 7. Documentation discipline

- Source is always **`.qmd`** in `docs/`.
  `README.md` is generated from
  `docs/README.qmd` (`project_utils/render_readme.sh`); never hand-edit
  `README.md`.
- `quarto render` runs `run_apidocs.sh`, `run_diagrams.sh`, and (for
  `render_readme.sh`) the exported docs output.
  Check `_site/` (not
  `docs/docs_web/`) is the publishable build when used as a website.
- Update the page's front-matter (`title`, `author`) - author = you,
  Sofia Billger Bergström.
- Keep internal links relative and verify them after moving files - e.g.
  `docs/plugins/...qmd` capitalization must match `_quarto.yml`.
- Add new capabilities to `TOOLS.qmd`; architecture decisions to
  `docs/…` and notes/
- Every plan page update is a real deliverable; do not ship \"TODO\" pages.

## 8. Testing

```bash
source .venv/bin/activate
ruff check .
ruff format --check .
 pytest -q
```

- Suite is offline; mock HITL, tools, MCP.
  Never live models.
- Use markers (`slow`, etc.) when adding expensive tests - slow tests must
  not run by default in CI.
- Common entry points for plugins: instead of `TestClient(create_app())`
  (which can hang waiting for stdio MCP processes), use cheap helpers
  like `chat_integration.list_chat_plugins()`.
- Sub-second feedback: use `py_compile` + `ruff` on touched files before
  waiting for a full run.
- `sqlite` tests must be per-operation; never share a `Connection` across
  threads.

## 9. Toolchain gotchas (observed)

- `keep_alive` MCP keep-stdio servers can block `pytest`; bound the run
  or avoid killing server processes inside tests.
- `agent-browser --enable react-devtools` is required for React component
  tracing during UI work.
- `git` remote operations (push, gh pr, merge) happen only on explicit
  user approval.
- Do not run `sudo`; ask Sofia.

## 10. Open a pull request

1. Keep it scoped - one logical piece.
2. Branch from `main`; no history rewriting shared.
3. Describe **what** changed and **why**; include test evidence and manual
   checks you performed.
4. Update docs if any public surface changed (new tool, env key, file path,
   mutation pattern).
5. Move plan files in `.opencode/plans/` if one tracks this work.
6. Wait for explicit approval before any push.

```markdown
## 11. Bootstrap checklist for a fresh checkout

- [ ] Python 3.12+, uv, `.venv` activated
- [ ] `uv pip install -e .`
- [ ] Web UI built (`npm run build`)
- [ ] Any plugin bundles built (`npm run build:ui`)
- [ ] Config directory resolves to the right project path
- [ ] `ruff check . && ruff format --check .` clean
- [ ] `pytest -q` passes
- [ ] Agent and docs updated
```
